# Billion Animals

> An OpenVet initiative for a billion animals with better medical histories and
> longer, healthier lives.

Billion Animals is an initiative of OpenVet. OpenVet is a comparative medical
intelligence company building a living map of disease, treatment, and recovery
across animal species. The mission is medicine for every animal on Earth.

## What the initiative is

The goal is a billion animals with better medical histories and longer,
healthier lives. It is a goal, not a count of records already collected. There
are two ambitions: a medical history for a billion animals, and a measurable
improvement in their lives.

An animal's history usually disappears when it changes clinics, moves cities,
or sees a specialist, and what one vet learns rarely reaches the next. A
history that follows the animal through life helps the people caring for it
make better decisions, and studied together those histories may show how
disease and recovery differ across animals, and what they share.

## How it begins

- OpenVet (https://openvet.ai) helps veterinarians during care.
- OpenAnimal (https://openanimal.ai) helps owners through daily life.

Together they are the start of a medical history that connects a
recommendation with what happened next. A billion animals will take far more
than one company.

## Why animal medicine matters to human medicine

- More than 6 in 10 known infectious diseases in people can spread from
  animals. Source: CDC, One Health: Zoonotic Diseases.
- Around 3 in 4 new or emerging infectious diseases in people come from
  animals. Source: CDC / WHO.
- Dogs develop cancers that closely resemble human ones, which is why the
  National Cancer Institute runs a comparative oncology program with
  veterinary clinics.

## Species

The initiative covers companion animals, production animals, large animals,
birds, aquatic species, reptiles, exotics and wildlife. Every animal is
entrusted to someone.
